markdown:
# #008. Multi-Period Production & Inventory Smoothing

<!-- section:scenario -->
A factory plans regular production `regular[t] <= regCap[t]`, overtime production `overtime[t] <= otCap[t]`, and end-of-period inventory `inventory[t] <= invCap` over $T$ periods ($t = 0, \dots, T-1$), starting with `initialInventory`.

In each period $t$, beginning stock plus total output must meet customer demand `demands[t]` with any surplus rolling into `inventory[t] >= 0`, and ending inventory after period $T-1$ must satisfy **`inventory[T-1] >= minFinalInventory`**. Minimize total regular (`regCost`), overtime (`otCost`), and holding (`holdCost`) costs.

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P008Input`)**:
  - `demands: number[]`, `regCap: number[]`, `otCap: number[]` — per-period demands and production caps
  - `invCap: number` — warehouse storage capacity in every period
  - `initialInventory: number`, `minFinalInventory: number` — boundary inventory levels
  - `regCost: number`, `otCost: number`, `holdCost: number` — unit regular, overtime, and holding costs
- **Output (`P008Output`)**:
  - `regular: number[]`, `overtime: number[]`, `inventory: number[]` — non-negative schedules of length $T$
  - `totalCost: number` — minimized total production + inventory cost

<!-- section:example -->
In Case 1 (`demands = [80, 140, 120, 70]`, `regCap = [100]*4`, `initialInventory = 10`, `minFinalInventory = 10`, `regCost = 20`, `otCost = 32`, `holdCost = 3`):

- Period 0 has spare regular capacity (`100` vs `80` demand), so producing at full `100` carries `30` units into Period 1 (`30 * 3 = 90` holding cost) instead of paying `+12`/unit overtime premium later (`+360`)!
- Combining pre-built inventory (`inventory = [30, 0, 0, 10]`) with targeted overtime (`overtime = [0, 10, 20, 0]`) yields **`totalCost = 8,680`**.

<!-- section:hint1 -->
Write the **inventory flow-conservation equation** connecting period $t-1$ to period $t$:
$$\text{inventory}[t] = \text{prevInventory} + \text{regular}[t] + \text{overtime}[t] - \text{demands}[t]$$
where `prevInventory = initialInventory` when $t = 0$ and `inventory[t - 1]` for $t \ge 1$.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Verify the boundary conditions carefully:
1. `0 <= regular[t] <= regCap[t]`, `0 <= overtime[t] <= otCap[t]`
2. `0 <= inventory[t] <= invCap` for $t < T - 1$, and for $t = T - 1$ impose **`minFinalInventory <= inventory[T-1] <= invCap`**.
3. Sum `regCost * regular[t] + otCost * overtime[t] + holdCost * inventory[t]` across all $t$.

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{r, o, I \ge 0} \quad & \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \left( c_r r_t + c_o o_t + c_h I_t \right) \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & I_t = I_{t-1} + r_t + o_t - d_t && \forall t \;\; (I_{-1} = I_{\text{init}}) \\
& 0 \le r_t \le R_t, \; 0 \le o_t \le O_t, \; 0 \le I_t \le I_{\max} && \forall t \\
& I_{T-1} \ge I_{\min,\text{end}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Inventory balance equations (`stock_next = stock_prev + inflow - outflow`) form a network-flow backbone appearing in supply chains, energy storage, and cash management!
